name: Breaking and Building
_what: Info film for the Breaking / Building domain: the Marchers and the Stillhold (violence and peace), the Unmakers and the Wrights of the New (ending and making), their homes, schools, costs, a figure or two each, the two arguments across the axes, and a close on the Marchward. Every string in lines, after, name and title is player-facing.

lines: Four peoples work where things break and where things are built.
Two argue about the fight, two about the made thing.
The Redline. Duelling floors in the squares, red lines on every boundary.
Duels settle law here, and children learn the Edge like their letters.
The Marchers hold that force will be used whether or not anyone is skilled, and that skill keeps a fight from spreading.
The Line takes the weapon rather than the life.
The Enders kept the craft and dropped the restraint.
Killing where the forms forbid costs a Marcher their standing.
And being good at violence does not make you right about when to use it.
Veyra of the Levelled Lance: twenty-two challenges on the Redline circuit, twenty-two stops.
What she fears is killing one.
Iseult of the Kept Word rides out of Hardline with forty who swore to her, not to a lord.
She repeats your promise back before she agrees.
The Stillhold. White walls, swept streets, gardens at every junction. No weapons, no raised voices, no violence in living memory.
Inside the gate stands a rack of surrendered weapons that nobody comes back for.
The calm is beautiful, and slightly wrong.
Here peace is a craft. Mediators bind truces to what both sides value. Interposers stand between, with their bodies.
The Quieters end a conflict by ending whoever will not stop.
Stillcraft is slow, and it is not gentle. The Price Shown leaves a reckoning in a person that they cannot unthink.
Vantia of the Stillhold does not advance. Nine wins in the Coliseum, and not one blow struck in attack.
Two she could not hold. She remembers both.
Both are honest that violence is coming. One answers by being excellent at it, the other by making it unnecessary.
The Scour. Towers taken down to clean stumps, the stone sorted and stacked beside them, the ground swept.
Things end whether or not anyone is skilled about it. Ruinwork finds where a thing wants to break, and takes it apart there.
To the Clearing Ground people bring what should end: a failing house, a life's work become a cage, a war.
Almost nobody thanks them.
The Enders-Well honour what they end. The Clearers halt the rot.
Up the road, the Scouring stopped asking whether a thing should end.
after: The asking was the last thing they ended.

lines: Ruinwork cannot touch the living, and it does not un-break. Undone is still gone.
Master Endmore licenses every demolition in the Scour, and asks each one the same question first: should this end?
The Forge-Eternal. Half-built cathedrals under scaffolding, cranes on the unfinished roofs.
None of it is done, and its people are so happy.
The Wrights hold that a finished thing has stopped being alive.
Makers build and mend. Improvers make a thing better than it was.
At the pure pole, the Ceaseless build over each other and over anything that is there.
Their making now includes things nobody asked for.
True making cannot be hurried. A masterwork can be made once, and a thing built to outlast you will.
Each season the best plan governs the Making. Planmaster Wyncote governs now, and hopes to lose to a plan he wishes he had drawn.
The Wright raises; the Unmaker ends. The same eye for structure, pointed opposite ways.
Each is the other's best consultant.
Every Reach is leaning harder into its own extreme. Travellers say the edges of the world are getting sharper.
Between the red lines and the white walls, the Marchward stays neutral, with a warlord's fires in sight of every window.
after: He was a Marcher once, protecting something.
